data.title: Slavs ambush a Frankish unit – a drawing by T. Humaj
data.excerpt: A Byzantine military manual describes how the Slavs fought: ambushes in thickets and defiles, hours spent under water breathing through hollow reeds, two short javelins apiece and arrows steeped in poison. Our collaborator Tomáš Humaj drew what such an attack might have looked like.
data.metaTitle: Slavs ambush a Frankish unit – T. Humaj
data.metaDescription: A drawing by T. Humaj after the account of Slavic tactics: ambushes in thickets, breathing under water through reeds, javelins and poisoned arrows.

mediaTexts.alt: A drawing of an ambush: horsemen and foot soldiers fighting in a field of grain

blocks.text: And because they lead a life of plunder, they (the Slavs) gladly prepare attacks upon their enemies in thickets, in defiles and on rocky heights. They are fond of using stratagems, sudden raids and pillaging… They bear being in the water to perfection, so that often some of them, when surprised by some danger, sink deep into the water and hold in their mouths long reeds, adapted for that purpose, hollow along their whole length and reaching up to the surface of the water. And lying on their backs in the depths, they breathe through them and endure in this way for several hours, arousing no one’s suspicion… As weapons each man carries two short javelins, some also fine shields… They also use wooden bows and short arrows steeped in poison… Because they do not suffer any dominion (over themselves) and hate one another, they know no battle order and are not fond of fighting in closed formations or of appearing in bare and level ground. And if it happens that they venture to join battle, they move a little forward with a war cry, and when their opponents give way before that cry, they rush fiercely upon them; if, however, they do not, they fall back…

children.text: What might such an attack have looked like? This scene (although probably from the 9th century) was created for our site by our collaborator Tomáš Humaj. What do you say?
